unresolved.problem: Says dissolved trona 'releases excess hydroxide ions (OH⁻)' directly. Trona contains carbonate/bicarbonate ions, which raise OH⁻ by hydrolysis; the salt does not release OH⁻ itself. The exemplar also calls the evaporated crystals 'the raw material for soda ash', which is acceptable, but then says 'useful as bleaching agent', which is loose. The OH⁻ statement is the scientific error.

Says 'Our body also has no bare metal surface to corrode' and gives only dilution and mucus as the reason. This is a weak non-sequitur, since the sufuria question asks why the drink is safe. More importantly, the prompt says the pitting is on the OUTSIDE of the pot, but the lemon-water was inside the pot per the lesson (outside pitting is inconsistent with the water being inside). The anchoring description says pitting on the outside where lemon-water sat inside.
